column1: # Scheduled maintenance, from the guidebook's table on p10.
# Cadence is in days. 0 means event-driven: it fires on a trigger, never on a
# clock, so it is never reported as overdue.
# Aggregate. One bounded maintenance branch beats a flood of autonomous pull
# requests nobody reviews. Security-critical fixes stay separate, because
# isolation is what makes them reviewable and shippable on their own.
# A fifth column, optional: a CHECK. For a cadence-0 row it is a command run in
# the checkout, exit 0 meaning not due and anything else meaning due — so an
# event-driven row can come due from reality instead of never. Rows with four
# columns keep working unchanged.
# The seeded graphify check compares file time to commit time at whole seconds,
# because that is how BSD find reads -newermt. A graph written in the same
# second as the last commit reads stale; nothing real does that.
# It excludes the cadence record, and that is not a loophole. Recording a run
# writes maintenance.log, and that write has to be committed for the cadence to
# survive the machine — so the act of recording the refresh invalidated the
# refresh, and the row was due again the moment it was satisfied. Measured on
# one project: due, refreshed, recorded, due, inside a single pull request.
# The exclusion is sound rather than convenient because the log is not in the
# graph's corpus at all — 103 entries, no .log and no .tsv among them — so a
# commit touching only it changes nothing the graph models. A check that says
# "the graph is behind the tree" must compare against the part of the tree the
# graph is a model OF.
# Any other commit still makes it due, which is the whole point: the row is a
# staleness detector and it is meant to fire when real content moves.
# The graph is looked for beside the repository's .git — `git rev-parse
# --git-common-dir` is `.git` in the checkout that holds it and the absolute
# path of that checkout's .git from any worktree — because a worktree has no
# graphify-out/ of its own, and a check keyed on the current directory read
# due in every worktree session whatever the graph's age. A due that is on
# almost always carries no information. The commit compared against is still
# the one the current checkout stands on, so a worktree that has moved past
# the graph is due, and the checkout the graph was built from is not.

column1: # Keyed on the checkout that holds the graph, and not on the tree the caller
# happens to be standing in. Those are the same thing in a plain checkout and
# different in a worktree, and the difference made this row a permanent DUE:
# any commit in a worktree is a commit the graph has not seen, sessions commit
# constantly, and sixteen of the seventeen session roots recorded for this
# project are worktrees. Measured at the top of one session: `due` from the
# worktree and `ok` from the checkout beside it, same graph, same second.
# This reverses the reading written here before it — that the commit compared
# against is the one the worktree stands on — and the argument is that the
# refresh that reading asks for cannot do what the DUE says is missing.
# graphify builds the graph from the checkout that holds it, so a refresh run
# while standing in a worktree models the HOLDING checkout's tree and not the
# worktree's unmerged work. It clears the row by moving a file's mtime, which
# is a change of status and not of what the graph models. A row that is on in
# almost every session, and whose remedy does not address the thing it names,
# is the status table this repository already keeps a lesson about.
# And prose is not in the key. Measured 2026-09-17 on felix: the graph was
# refreshed at 14:41 after an engine merge, a handoff-only merge landed at
# 14:54, and the row read due — and a second refresh could not clear it,
# because graphify writes nothing when no code changed, so the file's time
# never moves past a commit that touched nothing the graph models. The key is
# the last commit touching something other than this log and Markdown; a
# handoff section is the most common merge, and without this the row is
# permanently due, which is the shape the paragraph above already refuses.
graphify
column4: refresh the knowledge graph after a merge; it went fifteen days stale on one project while its row read event
column5: G="$(dirname "$(git rev-parse --git-common-dir)")"; test -n "$(find "$G/graphify-out/graph.json" -newermt "$(git log -1 --format=%cd --date=format-local:%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%S%z "$(git -C "$G" rev-parse HEAD)" -- . ":(exclude)projects/*/maintenance.log" ":(exclude)*.md")" 2>/dev/null)"
